title.narrative: Provision of emergency livelihood support to the most vulnerable drought-affected households in Afgoye

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project aims at providing emergency lifesaving food security and livelihood support to 1900 households /11400 persons (3142women, 2900 men, 2625 boys and 2733 girls) worst drought-affected agropastoral communities in the following 5 villages in Afgoye:ltbrgtMarerey, Sabiib,Canoole,Mordinle and Balguri by providing 700 of them with emergency unconditional cash transfers value of $55 per household/ month for three months covering approximately 70% of the food MEB inline with Food security cluster guidelines to support their immediate availability access to food, reduce food consumption gaps and mitigate negative coping mechanisms. The project will further ensure provision of agri-inputs to 1200 farmers HHs, consisting of 12 kgs sorghum, 10 kgs cowpea/ 12 kgs mung beans, vegetable seeds 350 grams, Maize seeds 10kg and farming tools consisting of hoe and forked hoe to enable them prepare their farms for planting. Additionally, 30 lead farmers will be trained on climate smart farming to equip them with requisite farming skills to cope with the climate challenges. The project targets 700 most vulnerable HHs with UCT and 1200HHs worst drought-affected farmers with Agri inputs. They will be selected in line with Vulnerability-based targeting to mimimize influence of gatekeepers. Beneficiaries selection will prioritize the most vulnerable minority groups identified from Horn Aid's RNA from the project targeted locations, particularly from Minority clans (somali Bantu, Yaxar, Tuni, and Bagadhi communities) with a particular focus on female-headed households, pregnant and lactating women (PLWs), children aged between six months and five years who are particularly vulnerable to health and nutrition-related risks and face a significant risk of malnutrition-related health complications, as well as families with persons with disabilities. Additionally, the project will strengthen women's participation by ensuring they are involved in all stages of the project, right from beneficiaries selection, implementation, monitoring, review and learning sessions. Moreover, the project monitoring will be guided by the organizational MEAL framework in close coordination and support by the government and key stakeholders. The project will strengthen protection with inclusive participation of socially marginalized communities, particularly minority clans, as well as PwDs who face risks of exclusion and isolation from aid. The project will prevent SEA, aid diversion, fraud, corruption by enhancing awareness and reporting channels such as CFM numbers for both OCHA and Horn Aid which will be clearly displayed in the project banners and posters at the distribution sites as well as during community engagement sessions, community social mobilization and project sensitization meetings which will further ensure information on beneficiary entitlements are clearly captured and articulated to the targeted beneficiaries. Horn Aid will strengthen coordination by actively participating in both national and state level/ Lower Shabelle Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) Cluster meetings, ABC, elders, local committees and MoHADM as well as humanitarian actors to limit duplications and strengthen synergies. The project will be implemented in close coordination and support with WASH, Health and Nutrition partners in Afgoye. The project comes at a time when there are significant funding shortfalls, while humanitarian needs are very dire and overwhelming as Afgoye is having 84,714 people in IPC phase 3/stressed and 11,427 in IPC chase 4/emergency (FSNAU post-Gu Assessment report of 23rd September 2025). Moreover and Rapid Needs Assessment conducted by Horn Aid from 11th - 13th December, 2025 confirmed that 3000 person (827 women, 763 men,719 girls and 691 boys) from the project target locations, that included Sabiib and Caanoole, which are conflict-affected and underserved despite prolonged exposure to drought and livelihood disruption.ltbrgtlt/pgt
